entities.title: In a HASD repository, requirements and architecture point at the .dev folders
entities.summary: requirements.md and architecture.md keep only what has no folder of their own, and point at the .dev records for capabilities, features, use cases, intended work and technical debt.
entities.context: The templates carried knowledge-driven development's marks. A repository that follows human-assisted software development keeps the same facts in .dev folders next to the code.
entities.decision: requirements.md says where the .dev records are and keeps what is out of scope and the open questions; architecture.md's known debt links to the debt records in the folders they concern; the README says so in step 4 of "Using the templates".

entities.title: What the other ten documents become in a HASD repository
entities.summary: Whether a repository that follows human-assisted software development still writes the other ten documents in Documentation/, or points them at the knowledge files that hold the same facts.
entities.context: The README's step 4 makes only requirements.md and architecture.md point at the .dev folders, and the AGENTS.md section it asks adopters to add says every deployable carries all twelve files. Human-assisted software development's knowledge catalogue maps every one of the twelve to a kind kept in .dev (business-plan.md to vision, stakeholders.md to stakeholders, risk-assessment.md to risks, deployment.md to delivery, cicd.md to pipeline, operations.md to runbooks and limitations, and so on), and its rule is one owner per fact. A HASD repository that follows both would hold, for example, its shutdown criteria in business-plan.md and in a vision record. The documents do not say which one owns the fact.

options.title: All twelve become pointers in a HASD repository
options.consequences: Each Documentation/ file names the .dev knowledge file that holds its subject and keeps a paragraph saying what is there; step 4 and the AGENTS.md section change to say so.

options.title: Only requirements and architecture point at .dev, as now
options.consequences: The other ten stay the source of truth for their subjects, and a HASD repository does not write the knowledge kinds adapted from them.

options.title: A HASD repository carries no Documentation/ directory
options.consequences: The knowledge files replace the twelve documents; the README and the AGENTS.md section say the convention applies only to repositories that do not follow HASD.

origin.description: Found while bringing processes in line with human-assisted software development, by reading the README against the knowledge catalogue.
